title: Adaptive benchmark orchestration and golden runbook for scheduling-aware performance
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an adaptive benchmarking orchestration layer and a golden-runbook that captures stable baseline runs across kernel variants, attention optimizations, and prefill/decode scheduling policies. The goal is to make perf comparisons reproducible, actionable for eng teams, and automatable in CI so we fail builds only on meaningful regressions. This ticket scopes the orchestration, data retention, statistical tests, and the golden baseline publication process.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestration component can run a workload matrix (model x kernel x attention x schedule) and produce normalized artifacts (latency, throughput, token-cost, quality) in under 6 hours for the standard suite
Golden baseline storage published to gs://redwood-perf/golden/runtime-1.19 with metadata and checksums for each run

CI integration: PRs touching runtime/kernel/attention paths trigger the suite in a lightweight mode and compare to golden baselines using pre-defined statistical tests; CI annotates regressions with magnitude and affected workloads
Regression policy documented: p95 latency regression >5% or throughput drop >7% or quality regression on golden prompts >1% leads to Blocked CI state
Runbook and playbook created for interpreting failures, triage steps, and automated rollback suggestions (model variant or kernel fallback).
tasks: Design matrix schema for workload combinations and environment tags (hw, cuda, driver)
Implement orchestration service that schedules runs on dedicated perf pool and captures KV-cache warmup traces
Add attention-variant toggles (e.g., flash, xformers, causal-approx) into the runner harness
Instrument harness to capture prefills vs decode step breakdown and per-token timings
Define and implement statistical comparison library (bootstrap CI-friendly) with configurable thresholds
Create CI job templates (full and lightweight) and wire into GitHub Actions and internal Jenkins
Author golden-runbook doc with triage checklist, example PR annotations, and rollback recipes

2025-02-24 - Asha Patel: Decided on statistical test: 10 bootstrap samples with 95% confidence for p50/p95; quality checks use token-level agreement on golden prompts with a tolerance of 1.0% absolute delta.

2025-02-28 - Liam O'Connor: Integrated attention-variant toggles. Observed a 3.6% p95 improvement using flash-attn on medium-long sequences for int8 kernels. Captured artifacts and updated golden candidate for runtime-1.19.

2025-03-03 - PM review (Riley Chen): Reviewed the runbook. Request to add customer-facing summary and a short-form incident blurb template for SEs to reference when contacting customers after a perf regression.

2025-03-04 - Liam O'Connor: CI lightweight job implemented. Runs a representative subset (3 models x 2 kernels x 2 sequence lengths) in under 20 minutes; PR: #2598. Next: hook up automatic CI annotations on regression failures.
notes: We must ensure deterministic seeds for decoding when measuring quality to avoid noise from sampling; top-k/top-p stochastic modes excluded from golden quality checks.
Prefill scheduling tests should capture both single-request heavy prefill and many small-prefill mixed workloads to exercise KV cache eviction policies.
Consider adding a synthetic microbenchmark that isolates attention memory bandwidth vs kernel compute to help narrow regressions.
Long-term: expose a perf-profile API so product teams can request lightweight ad-hoc runs for customer incidents.
